old: "content": "Use simple invitation forms such as ¿*Quieres* *venir*? and ¿Te *gustaría* *venir*? to invite someone. Positive responses can use *Sí*, *claro*, *Me gustaría* or *Sí*, *quiero* *ir*. Keep the invitation focused on the event, time or activity. In this lesson the main aim is making and accepting invitations naturally."
new: "content": "Use *¿Quieres* + infinitive? to invite someone: *¿Quieres venir a la fiesta?* You know *querer* and *poder* from Unit 10, so you can also ask *¿Puedes* + infinitive? to check that the person is free: *¿Puedes venir el sábado?* To accept, say *Sí, claro* and add *Quiero ir* or *Puedo ir*. Keep the invitation focused on the event, time or activity."
why: 08-01 teaches ¿Te gustaría…? (polite-softening, Unit 26) and its table is about ya/todavía no: rewrite with quieres/puedes

new: "content": "*¿Quieres venir?* asks whether the person wants to come; *¿Puedes venir?* asks whether they are free. Both are friendly invitations, and *Sí, claro* answers either one."

old: "content": "Use *ya* with the *pretérito* *perfecto* to say that something has already happened or has already been done. *Ya* normally appears before the participle or after the auxiliary: *Ya he preparado la cena*. In invitation contexts, it can explain that you have already made plans or preparations."
new: "content": "You know *ya* with the *pretérito perfecto* from Unit 2: *Ya he preparado la cena*. Here you use it to answer an invitation: when you have already made plans or preparations, say so. *Ya* comes before *he* or *hemos*, and the participle follows."
